tour.name: Great Ocean Road Private Day Trip from Melbourne: the Twelve Apostles & Loch Ard Gorge
tour.subtitle: One of the world's great coastal drives in a private day with a local guide and car: the surf beaches of Torquay and Bells Beach, the Memorial Arch, wild koalas at Kennett River, the rainforest of the Great Otway National Park, and the limestone stacks of the Twelve Apostles and Loch Ard Gorge at sunset.

A rainforest walk among giant tree ferns in the Otways
tour.overview:
Between 1919 and 1932, some 3,000 soldiers returned from the First World War carved a road along the cliffs of south-west Victoria, by hand, with picks and shovels. The Great Ocean Road, 243 kilometres long, is the largest war memorial in the world and one of its most beautiful drives, ending at the Twelve Apostles, giant limestone stacks carved by the Southern Ocean.

This private day trip takes you along the road with a local guide and a car, stopping for surf beaches, wild koalas and a rainforest walk, and reaching the Apostles in the softer afternoon light. A private car lets you return quickly inland.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 12 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Melbourne
• Type: private tour with local guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Torquay and Bells Beach.
• The Memorial Arch.
• Kennett River and Apollo Bay.
• The Great Otway National Park.
• The Twelve Apostles and Loch Ard Gorge.

WHY THIS WORKS
It is a long day; a private car and guide make it comfortable, with stops when you want them and a faster inland return.

WHO IT SUITS
Nature lovers, families, photographers and couples.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
To take it slowly, ask us for a 2-day version with a night in Apollo Bay or Port Campbell.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The coast is exposed and often windy, even in summer: bring a windproof jacket. A helicopter flight over the Apostles can be added.

days.name: Torquay, the Memorial Arch, Kennett River, the Otways, the Twelve Apostles and Loch Ard Gorge
days.description:
What to expect: the coastal road and its cliffs, beaches, koalas and rainforest, with a local guide, private car and meals.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 7:30 and drive to Torquay, the start of the road and the home of Australian surfing, and Bells Beach, where the world's oldest professional surfing contest is held each Easter. Morning tea is served by the sea. You pass under the Memorial Arch at Eastern View, dedicated to the soldiers who built the road, and follow the cliffs to Lorne.

At Kennett River, you look for wild koalas sleeping in the eucalyptus trees, often with colourful king parrots and rosellas around you. Lunch is at Apollo Bay, a fishing town. The road then turns inland through the Great Otway National Park, where a short walk leads through a cool temperate rainforest of giant tree ferns and myrtle beech.

In the afternoon you reach the Twelve Apostles, limestone stacks up to 45 metres high standing in the surf, of which fewer than twelve now remain. You walk the boardwalks to the viewpoints, then visit Loch Ard Gorge, named after a ship wrecked here in 1878 with only two young survivors, and the Razorback. You return to Melbourne by the faster inland road, arriving at about 20:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up in Melbourne.
09:00 – Torquay and Bells Beach, morning tea.
10:00 – Memorial Arch.
11:00 – Kennett River koalas.
12:15 – Lunch in Apollo Bay.
13:45 – Otway rainforest walk.
15:15 – Twelve Apostles.
16:30 – Loch Ard Gorge.
17:15 – Drive back to Melbourne.
20:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Sunset at the Apostles can be arranged in summer; the day then ends later.
• A helicopter flight over the Apostles can be added.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, local guide, morning tea, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: helicopter flight, tips.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How long is the day?
faq.answer: About 12 hours, with roughly 6 hours of driving. The return is by the inland road.

faq.question: Will we see koalas?
faq.answer: Very likely at Kennett River, in the trees. They are wild, so sightings are never guaranteed.

faq.question: Are meals included?
faq.answer: Yes, morning tea and lunch in Apollo Bay.

faq.question: Can we see the sunset at the Apostles?
faq.answer: Yes, on request, especially in summer when sunset is late.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Child seats are provided free of charge on request. Breaks are planned.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The main Apostles viewpoints are accessible; Loch Ard Gorge has stairs to the beach.

faq.question: Can we do it in 2 days?
faq.answer: Yes. We recommend a night in Apollo Bay or Port Campbell to enjoy it slowly.

faq.question: Can we add the Grotto and London Bridge?
faq.answer: Yes, on the 2-day version or a longer day.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Layers and a windproof jacket, comfortable shoes, a hat and sun cream.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. December to March is warmest; winter brings dramatic seas.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not expected in Australia, where wages are higher, but it is always appreciated for excellent service.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
